stories.name: Celestica Draws New Stakes From LaSalle, Burnham
stories.summary: LaSalle St. Investment Advisors LLC disclosed new positions in Celestica, Texas Instruments, CSX and Chevron during the second quarter, signaling active portfolio expansion across technology, industrial and energy stocks. In Celestica, LaSalle established a new stake of 2,982 shares valued at about $1.09 million, while Celestica also saw a separate 2,500-share purchase by Burnham & Co LLC. In Texas Instruments, LaSalle bought 1,973 shares for roughly $588,000. In CSX, LaSalle took a new position of 33,225 shares worth about $1.58 million. In Chevron, LaSalle accumulated 6,295 shares valued at around $1.04 million. Separately, Celestica’s filings noted large prior moves by other institutions, and Texas Instruments reported senior executives selling sizable blocks of stock, including the CEO, highlighting ongoing insider activity alongside institutional moves.
keyPoints: Burnham & Co LLC bought 2,500 Celestica shares in the second quarter, valued at approximately $912,000, signaling continued interest from other institutional investors in Celestica alongside LaSalle St.'s new position.

Celestica insiders also traded heavily during the period: CEO Robert Mionis sold 23,496 shares on August 13 at an average price of $362.39 (about $8.51 million), and CFO Mandeep Chawla sold 16,117 shares on August 4 at about $369.32 per share (about $5.95 million), contributing to a substantial reduction in CEO ownership.

Texas Instruments drew additional hedge-fund activity in Q2: LaSalle St. bought 1,973 shares (about $588,000), and overall 84.99% of TXN stock is owned by hedge funds and institutional investors, with other funds opening new positions (Mystic Asset Management, Advisors Preferred, Oxford Financial Group, Kilter Group, and D L Carlson Investment Group) during the quarter.

stories.name: Ryanair Holdings Stake Slashed 28.1% by Eagle
stories.summary: Multiple institutional investors shifted their Ryanair Holdings PLC stakes in the second quarter, with Eagle Global Advisors reducing its holding by 28.1% to 46,000 shares (about $2.98 million). Other funds adjusted in the opposite direction or with smaller changes, including Milford Funds Ltd. increasing its stake by 25.4% to 1,263,847 shares (roughly $81.8 million), Assetmark Inc. rising by 5.4% to 466,733 shares, W.G. Shaheen & Associates up 1.6% to 219,157 shares, U S Global Investors up 34.1% to 139,753 shares, and Ascentis Wealth Management LLC expanding dramatically to 5,115 shares after a large percentage increase. Collectively, institutional investors owned a substantial portion of Ryanair, around 43.66% of the stock across the reporting entities. In addition to these moves, Hudson Edge Investment Partners cut its Ryanair stake by 5.7% to 921,550 shares, reflecting ongoing reevaluations of the carrier’s exposure within diversified portfolios. The pattern shows a mix of reductions and new allocations among major funds, signaling varied strategies and views on Ryanair’s near-term prospects.
keyPoints: Hudson Edge Investment Partners reduced its Ryanair stake to 921,550 shares, representing about 8.2% of its investment portfolio and making Ryanair its 3rd biggest holding; the stake was valued at roughly $59.67 million.
Eagle Global Advisors cut its Ryanair position by 28.1% in the second quarter, selling 18,000 shares and ending with 46,000 shares worth about $2.978 million.
Assetmark Inc. raised its Ryanair stake by 5.4% in the second quarter to 466,733 shares, after purchasing 23,906 additional shares; the position was valued at roughly $30.221 million.

stories.name: Arista Networks Sees Major Funds Expand 2Q Stakes
stories.summary: Several institutional investors increased their positions in Arista Networks during the second quarter, led by Fire Capital Management LLC, which boosted its stake 17.2% to 18,116 shares (about 1.3% of its portfolio) for roughly $3.08 million. Acumen Wealth Advisors LLC followed with a 184.8% rise to 20,278 shares, valued at about $3.445 million. Other firms also expanded holdings, including Lighthouse Financial Services, Bensler LLC, QRG Capital Management, Reaves W H & Co., and Jefferies Financial Group, with overall institutional ownership around 82.47%. In addition to this activity, major insider movement occurred as Andreas Bechtolsheim sold 300,000 Arista shares on August 5, leaving him with about 181.1 million shares valued at roughly $36.8 billion. First Community Trust NA added 22,729 shares in Q2, worth about $3.861 million, making ANET around 1.7% of its portfolio and its 10th largest holding. The reporting across filings and disclosures underscores sustained institutional appetite for Arista Networks amid ongoing trading and stake adjustments by both hedge funds and corporate insiders.
keyPoints: Andreas Bechtolsheim sold 300,000 Arista Networks shares on August 5, leaving him with about 181,143,048 shares valued at roughly $36.83 billion; the sale totaled $60.99 million at an average price of $203.30 per share.

Arista's CEO Jayshree Ullal sold 767,029 shares on August 5, reducing her stake to 16,387,981 shares, valued at about $3.30 billion, with the sale totaling approximately $154.34 million at an average price of $201.22.
Norges Bank added a new stake in Arista Networks during the fourth quarter, in a position worth approximately $1.56 billion.

stories.name: Celestica stock soars after multi-billion equity offering
stories.summary: Celestica’s stock has surged as investors look past the recent equity offering and focus on its growing role in AI infrastructure, supported by a strengthened balance sheet and strong quarterly results. The $3 billion capital raise is viewed as de-risking expansion plans and enabling higher spending on data-center capacity and 800G/1.6T networking programs for hyperscalers, with 2026 guidance raised and analysts bullish on the long-term AI buildout. Analysts have amplified the rally, with upbeat targets and emphasis on Celestica’s niche in AI networking and its tight links to major cloud and AI customers. Yet concerns persist about shareholder dilution, heavy reliance on a few large customers, and potential volatility if growth or AI demand cools, alongside notable insider selling activity. The broader context remains a favorable backdrop for cash-generative AI infrastructure stocks, as improving demand and margins support a positive outlook despite the stock-specific risks.
keyPoints: Insider selling activity at Celestica has been substantial: CEO Robert Mionis sold 299,057 shares for an estimated $113.65 million and CFO Mandeep Chawla sold 34,000 shares for about $13.07 million over the last six months, with 135 insider sales and no reported purchases.
The company is not only raising guidance but is seeing dramatic implied growth in 2026, with revenue expected to jump 65% and adjusted earnings per share up 87%.

Celestica's revenue mix shows scale in AI networking: Connectivity & Cloud Solutions generates about US$12.3 billion, while Advanced Technology Solutions adds roughly US$3.3 billion, underscoring the business lines driving AI infrastructure demand.

stories.name: CLS Holdings posts wider H1 loss
stories.summary: CLS Holdings posted a substantial H1 2026 statutory loss after tax of 69.6 million pounds and widened pre-tax loss to 72.5 million, with EPRA earnings sliding to 2.7 pence per share. Revenue fell to 64.3 million pounds and net rental income declined 13.1% as disposals, expiries, and tenant issues weighed on the business, while portfolio valuations dropped 4.6% in local currency and EPRA net tangible assets per share declined 11.5%. The group completed or agreed disposals totaling about 201 million pounds since early 2025, kept vacancy stable at 14.5%, and reduced net debt by around 44 million pounds. However, loan-to-value rose to 51.6% as valuations declined and debt costs averaged about 3.9%. The company does not plan an interim dividend and is prioritising disposals, refinancing, and selective investment to reshape the portfolio and strengthen its balance sheet, guiding FY26 EPS of 4.6 to 5.5 pence. Management remains focused on leasing, disposals, and refinancing across its UK, Germany, and France portfolio as market conditions potentially improve.
keyPoints: H1 2026 saw £56.8m of property sales completed, with disposals progress continuing and £5.7m of contracted rent secured across 57 new leases and renewals.
Around 89% of CLS’s 2026 refinancing activity has been completed or agreed, with average debt costs around 3.9%.
CFO Patrick Symons said net rental income was hit by more than £200m of disposals since early 2025, plus expiries at the New Printing House Square block and German tenant insolvencies.

stories.name: Celestica Stock Falls 12% on Aug 6 Amid Growth Outlook Concerns
stories.summary: Celestica’s stock moves reflect a mix of optimism around its growing role in AI data-center infrastructure and concerns about cash flow conversion and capital allocation. Market mood has turned cautious as investors weigh potential deceleration in enterprise IT spending against Celestica’s expanding CCS exposure and elevated valuation, contributing to profit-taking after prior gains. Despite a recent earnings beat and expectations of higher 2027 growth from strong customer demand, the company’s shares faced pressure from a multi-billion share offering and a notable after-hours drop, signaling short-term selling despite buoyant longer-term sentiment. Analysts remain broadly positive, with several like TD Securities upgrading to strong-buy and raising targets, while overall consensus on Celestica remains favorable even as some metrics, such as free cash flow relative to reported profit, raise concerns about underlying profitability. Critics also highlight that Celestica’s accrual ratio implies cash flow generation trails profits, suggesting investors should monitor free cash flow conversion despite recent growth and potential upside from AI-related programs.
keyPoints: Analysts warn that the AI-driven data-center hardware cycle may be normalizing, with industry dynamics suggesting a deceleration in enterprise IT spending and a potential de-rating of Celestica's premium valuation.
Celestica reported Q2 results with C$3.61 earnings per share on revenue of C$6.68 billion, along with a return on equity of 50.28% and a net margin of 7.15%.
TD Securities upgraded Celestica to a Strong Buy and raised the price target to C$430 (from C$350), signaling continued bullish broker sentiment.

stories.name: CNA Financial CAO Franzetti sells 22,656 shares
stories.summary: CNA Financial Corp.’s chief accounting officer, Daniel Paul Franzetti, sold 22,656 CNA shares on August 4, 2026, at an average price of $53.09, for about $1.2028 million. After the sale, Franzetti directly owned 68,032 CNA shares, a roughly 25% reduction in his holdings. The Form 4 filing describes the transaction as a sale in an open market or private transaction, with no pre-arranged trading plan indicated. In the broader insider activity, CNA insiders have had two open-market stock sales in the past six months and no purchases. CNA stock traded around $52.93 on the day, coming after the company’s quarterly earnings of $1.19 per share, which beat estimates, and amid a mixed broader trading backdrop. Separate coverage notes ongoing institutional repositioning among major investors in Q1 2026 as part of CNA’s evolving investor base.
keyPoints: The Form 4 indicates Franzetti's sale occurred in multiple trades at prices ranging from $53.05 to $53.31 per share, for an average price of $53.09.
CNA's quarterly results showed revenue of $3.83 billion and earnings per share of $1.19, with revenue beating consensus estimates of about $2.97 billion.

Institutional investor activity in Q1 2026 reflected notable portfolio moves, including Millennium Management removing 577,247 shares, UBS removing 554,595 shares, First Trust Advisors adding 540,448 shares, Northwestern Mutual removing 483,079 shares, Two Sigma adding 344,489 shares, AQR adding 253,489 shares, and Point72 removing 245,623 shares.

stories.name: Celestica stock climbs after hedge fund stake increase
stories.summary: Celestica has seen notable institutional buying, with Verus Capital Partners expanding its stake by more than 1,000% and other funds such as Renaissance Technologies, CIBC Asset Management, Norges Bank, Marietta Investment Partners, and BW Gestão de Investimentos increasing their positions in CLS. Gateway Wealth Partners also boosted its Celestica holding by over 370%, underscoring ongoing appetite from investors. In price action, Royal Bank of Canada lifted its target to 450 and maintained an outperform rating, contributing to a roughly 7.8% intraday rise after the upgrade, while other analysts including JPMorgan, Stifel, Wolfe Research, and Susquehanna issued higher targets or more favorable ratings. The Q2 results reinforced the growth narrative, with Celestica posting strong revenue around $4.7 billion, an adjusted EPS of about $2.54, and management signaling an improved 2026 outlook as demand from hyperscalers and AI infrastructure strengthens. Across reports, analysts have raised price targets and reinforced bullish sentiment on CLS, reflecting confidence in the company's execution and growth trajectory. Institutional investors reportedly own about 67% of the stock, highlighting broad participation in Celestica’s potential.
keyPoints: Renaissance Technologies LLC bought a new stake in Celestica during the 1st quarter, valued at approximately $68,952,000.
Norges Bank purchased a new Celestica stake in the 4th quarter, valued at roughly $456,511,000.
CIBC Asset Management Inc. increased its Celestica stake by 7.7% in the 4th quarter, now owning 436,922 shares worth about $129,499,000.

stories.name: Trader Alerts Highlight Mixed Earnings Across Sectors
stories.summary: A Benzinga Pro batch of trade alerts summarizes quarterly results and outlooks across energy services, electronics manufacturing, software, and tech hardware, signaling a broad mix of earnings momentum for traders. Companies such as Core Laboratories and Benchmark Electronics report GAAP and adjusted earnings per share alongside revenue guidance, with ranges to compare against consensus estimates. PTC, Lam Research, and Sensata Technologies contribute guidance or results that influence next-quarter expectations, highlighting volatility in semis-related and industrial names. Insperity and Tenable Holdings add adjusted EPS figures that beat or approach estimates while guiding on upcoming quarters, reflecting a tech services and cybersecurity tilt. FMC and other industrials round out the set with forward-looking sales or earnings guidance, reinforcing cautious optimism amid varied guidance. Overall, the collection mirrors real-time market intelligence aimed at helping traders parse which companies are delivering versus expectations across multiple sectors.
keyPoints: Core Laboratories projects Q3 GAAP EPS of 0.12 to 0.20 and revenue of $128 million to $135 million, versus consensus of about $0.16 and $131.33 million.
PTC guides for Q4 adjusted EPS of 1.63 to 2.21 and sales of $630 million to $690 million, versus consensus of about $1.81 for EPS and $649.5 million for revenue.
Benchmark Electronics reports Q3 GAAP EPS of 0.51 to 0.57 and Q3 adjusted EPS of 0.76 to 0.82, both topping estimates, with sales guidance of 0.755 to 0.795 billion.

stories.name: Cadence Q2 Revenue Up; Celestica Outlook Updated
stories.summary: Cadence Design Systems posted a strong Q2 2026 with revenue of $1.584 billion, up 24.2% year over year and a record backlog of $8.1 billion, as AI-driven design activity and demand in data centers and automotive support expanded bookings. Non-GAAP EPS reached $2.11, beating estimates, and management highlighted continued momentum in AI for design and design for AI, with agentic AI seen as a durable tailwind expanding the addressable market. Celestica reported Q2 2026 results above expectations, with revenue of $4.7 billion and adjusted EPS of $2.54, and raised full-year guidance to 2026 revenue of $20.5 billion and adjusted EPS of $11.30, while boosting free cash flow to $600 million and maintaining capex at $1 billion to support capacity. The company cited stronger AI/infrastructure demand, 800G networking programs, and multiyear visibility with hyperscalers as drivers of margin improvement and optimistic 2027 growth, with expectations that earnings growth will outpace revenue growth as margins expand. Several Celestica notes reiterate that 2027 revenue growth could exceed the year’s pace, supported by collaborations (OpenAI and Broadcom) and upcoming mass production of 1.6 terabit networking programs in 2026. Cadence’s results and Celestica’s outlook collectively reflect a broader industry shift toward AI-enabled compute infrastructure and AI-driven design/production cycles, underscoring sustained demand across EDA and electronics manufacturing services.
keyPoints: Cadence Design Systems reported double-digit growth across all product groups in Q2 2026, signaling broad-based demand beyond AI-specific applications.
Cadence also highlighted momentum on AI for Design and Design for AI, with 'strong early traction' for its AI Super-Agent portfolio as customers ramp up simulations and tooling.
Celestica posted margin improvement with an 8.2% adjusted operating margin, driven by improved operating leverage across its segments.

stories.name: Celestica Shares Dip as CFO Sells 17,000
stories.summary: Celestica Inc. shares have seen recent activity from institutional investors, with Calamos Advisors trimming its stake by about 72% in Q1, while other managers added small positions, underscoring mixed but ongoing interest. Market sentiment among analysts remains broadly favorable, with a consensus rating of Buy from multiple firms and several price targets suggesting upside from current levels. Reports show ongoing research coverage citing strong earnings growth expectations, with multiple firms maintaining or raising price targets and rating sophistication across banks and investment houses. A growth-focused analysis highlights Celestica’s diversified segments in Advanced Technology Solutions and Connectivity & Cloud Solutions, positioning the company to benefit from AI infrastructure spending and cloud-buildout, supported by solid profitability metrics. However, valuation concerns persist, as recent analysis indicates the stock trades well above intrinsic value estimates, with insider selling signaling potential source of caution for new buyers. The combination of bullish ratings, rising targets, and structural growth drivers is tempered by notable overvaluation and insider activity signaling ongoing vigilance for investors.
keyPoints: Beyond Calamos Advisors’ 71.8% stake reduction, several other institutions initiated new Celestica positions in late-2023 to early-2026: UBS Asset Management Americas LLC opened a new Q4 stake worth about $28,000; Ascentis Independent Advisors started a new Q1 position around $29,000; Swiss RE Ltd. opened a Q4 position about $29,000; Cullen Frost Bankers Inc. added a Q4 stake near $30,000; and Sittner & Nelson LLC established a new Q4 position around $31,000.

Analyst price targets and ratings have been raised by multiple banks in recent coverage, including Goldman Sachs reiterating Buy with a $475 target; UBS raised its target to $400 and moved to Neutral; Bank of America lifted its target to $430 with a Buy rating; Stifel Nicolaus set a $445 target; Weiss Ratings upgraded Celestica from Buy (b-) to Buy (b).

Market-wide analyst sentiment shows a strong Buy bias: a consensus of Buy from 18 of 22 covering firms (with 2 Holds and 2 Strong Buys) and an average one-year price objective around $427.42, according to MarketBeat; coverage notes include target adjustments from multiple firms.

stories.name: MDA Space Plans Majority CLS Stake in Global Geointelligence Expansion
stories.summary: MDA Space has entered into a firm and irrevocable offer to acquire a majority stake in CLS, a global AI-driven Earth observation and satellite IoT services provider, with the deal valuing CLS at €567 million in cash for about 70% ownership and leaving the CNES with roughly 30%. CLS is expected to generate about €286 million in revenue in 2026, and the combined group would expand MDA Space’s footprint with roughly 40 sites across 19 countries, aiming to double recurring revenue and enhance profitability and cash generation. The acquisition is slated to close after regulatory and stakeholder approvals in a timeline that could stretch into late 2026 or 2027, aligning with CLS’s global growth and MDA Space’s strategic expansion. To fund the deal, MDA Space announced a bought deal share offering of about 20 million shares at $35.60 to raise roughly $712 million in gross proceeds, with banks able to sell up to 15% more, while noting the financing is not conditional on the CLS transaction and that dilution and valuation overhang could weigh on the stock until closing and deployment clarity emerges. MDA Space’s leadership reframes the transaction as creating a vertically integrated geospatial services leader with broad government and commercial go-to-market capabilities and a comprehensive multi-sensor data product suite.
keyPoints: The deal is framed as creating one of the largest space-based geointelligence businesses in the world, expanding MDA Space’s capability with CLS’s AI-driven Earth observation data and services across a broad multi-sensor portfolio.
CLS reportedly serves more than 14,000 customers across around 150 countries, highlighting the scale and global reach that MDA Space would acquire.
There could be an additional €198 million of debt to be posted by MDA Space to pay off existing obligations before the CLS deal closes, adding to the financial complexity of the transaction.

stories.name: AADX Stock Climbs 2.36%; Four-Week Surge Continues
stories.summary: MDA Space Ltd. has seen its stock price rise to about $42.11, trading well above its 52-week low and near its high, while GuruFocus flags an 86.5% overvaluation relative to its GF Value estimate. The GF Score stands at 49/100, suggesting a mix of strengths and weaknesses across financial metrics, with financial strength highlighted as a point of reference. The stock also carries a high P/E ratio of 73.0x, roughly 89% above its 5-year median, reinforcing concerns about valuation. Insider activity has been minimal, with no insider transactions reported in the last three months. Beyond price, MDA Space is expanding its international aerospace footprint through recent satellite contract wins, a strategic acquisition, and participation in large government radar and space infrastructure programs in Canada. The company maintains a broad portfolio of space tech, including satellite communications, Canadarm3, RADARSAT-2, Earth observation services, and other robotics and defense-oriented solutions for governments and commercial clients.
keyPoints: MDA Space's current price of $42.11 sits near the upper end of its 52-week range ($15.00–$49.37).

MDA Space’s product portfolio includes MDA AURORA (software-defined digital satellite products) and MDA SKYMAKER (space robotics), expanding capabilities beyond traditional satellite communications to software and robotics.
The company rebranded from MDA Ltd. to MDA Space Ltd. in May 2024, reflecting a corporate name change.

stories.name: Celestica Names Dorwart President Connectivity Cloud Solutions
stories.summary: Celestica appointed Steven Dorwart as President of its Connectivity and Cloud Solutions segment, taking over from retiring executive Jason Phillips who will stay on as an advisor. The stock has surged over the past year, delivering a 1-year return of about 137% and still showing momentum despite a softer 30-day run. Analysts have the stock as roughly 23% undervalued based on their fair value, while cautioning about exposure to a few hyperscaler customers and ongoing AI and cloud investment risks. GuruFocus, for July 6, 2026, flags the shares as significantly overvalued relative to its GF Value and notes a high price-to-earnings multiple versus its historical median. Celestica also plans to release its second-quarter 2026 financial results with a webcast/conference call, as disclosed by the company. Additionally, multiple large investors have adjusted their holdings, with a broad pattern of stake trimming among major holders in Celestica, suggesting cautious positioning around the stock.
keyPoints: Celestica posted a roughly 90-day return of 20.5% with a 30-day decline near 4%, signaling recent momentum but near-term weakness despite the longer-term uptrend.
Analysts’ fair value estimate implies upside: CA$648.86 per share versus the CA$498.11 current price, suggesting a potential increase from the present level.
GuruFocus notes the stock as 166.4% overvalued based on GF Value (price of about $350.20 vs GF Value of $131.47) with a P/E of 42.4x, well above the 5-year median of 16.4x.

stories.name: Celestica Shares Rise on Positive Earnings Outlook
stories.summary: Celestica remains a focal point for investors as analysts highlight strong earnings revisions, robust growth prospects in AI data centers, and a bullish sentiment around its AI and high-tech manufacturing services. The company has seen upward revisions to earnings estimates and has been lauded with multiple buy ratings and high price targets from major banks, underpinning a perception of expanding margins and revenue growth. Stock movements across articles show a mixture of rallies and strong demand for CLS shares, with broker forecasts repeatedly signaling upside from current levels as the AI spending boom translates into demand for Celestica’s contract manufacturing and infrastructure services. Analysts point to Celestica’s leadership role in building and assembling hardware for hyperscalers, telecoms, and semiconductor ecosystems, as well as a favorable risk-reward balance given its position in AI infrastructure. While some articles note a surge in earnings expectations and multiple upgrades, investors are advised to watch for execution in the company’s ATS and CCS segments and the pace of AI-related contract wins that could drive further upside. Celestica’s stock remains a well-followed play on the AI hardware cycle, trading at premium targets that reflect optimism about its long-term growth trajectory and exposure to data-center and AI-related demand.
keyPoints: Zacks highlights Celestica’s near-term earnings potential with Q1 EPS of $2.28 (up ~64% YoY) and full-year EPS of $10.16 (up ~67.9% YoY), with the 30-day consensus unchanged.

Major banks have issued bullish targets: Goldman Sachs maintains a Buy with a $475 target, Bank of America lifts to a $430 target, TD Securities boosts to a $430 target (from $350), and UBS sets $400 with Neutral; MarketBeat shows a consensus near $427.42.

Long-term growth expectations are notable, with projections for revenue and adjusted earnings to more than double between FY25 and FY27; and sentiment remains skewed toward Strong Buys, with 16 of 19 broker ratings labeled as Strong Buys per Zacks.

stories.name: CEO Robert Mionis sells $21.6M Celestica shares
stories.summary: Celestica CEO Robert Mionis sold 55,768 shares of the company’s stock on June 16 at an average price of about $386.96, for roughly $21.6 million in proceeds, cutting his direct holdings by 41.52%. The filing indicates the sale was carried out under a Rule 10b5-1 plan adopted on March 11, 2026. Mionis also reported additional sales around the same period, including 66,056 shares on June 15 and 18,176 shares on June 17 at average prices of about $400.06 and $385.17. On Wednesday, Celestica shares were down about $1.70 to around $380.31 on heavy trading volume versus average. Analyst coverage referenced in the reports includes both rating/target changes and maintaining a range of outlooks for the stock.
keyPoints: After selling 55,768 shares on June 16, Celestica CEO Robert Mionis reported he would still directly own 78,560 shares, valued at about $30,399,577.60 (down 41.52% from before the sale).

On the stock’s down day, Celestica traded 1,189,950 shares versus an average volume of 2,133,640; the report also listed technical/valuation metrics including a 50-day moving average of $380.87 and a 200-day moving average of $325.89, plus financial ratios such as a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.36 and a beta of 2.02.

Analyst coverage cited in the filings/reports included specific rating and price-target actions: TD Cowen upgraded Celestica from “hold” to “buy” and raised its target from $350 to $430; JPMorgan increased its target from $410 to $425 and rated the stock “overweight.” Separately, another report noted Zacks lowered the shares from “strong-buy” to “hold,” and Bank of America raised its target from $400 to $430 with a “buy” rating.

stories.name: Richardson Celestica $300M Expansion Plans, 2,300 Jobs
stories.summary: Celestica, a Canadian electronics manufacturing services firm, is expanding its Telecom Parkway campus in Richardson by renewing leases for two existing buildings and adding a new 343,000-square-foot facility now under construction, bringing its total footprint to about 1 million square feet through 2036. The company plans to invest roughly $300 million over the next two years to fund tenant improvements and new equipment tied to its advanced manufacturing work for AI data center infrastructure. The expansion is expected to retain nearly 400 existing jobs and create about 2,300 new permanent positions in that same timeframe. Richardson is supporting the project with a $3 million tenant improvement grant under a framework tied to long-term occupancy, capital spending, and job creation. The announcement also follows Celestica’s recent confirmation of additional manufacturing plans in Fort Worth, where the city approved tax incentives for a separate project.
keyPoints: Celestica also signed a 10-year lease for its 600,000-square-foot manufacturing hub at 2801 Telecom Parkway, with plans to expand into an additional 343,000 square feet of office space by next year—details that weren’t included in the summary.

The Telecom Parkway site has a notable tenant history: it previously served as Fujitsu’s North American headquarters, with Fujitsu later selling the office to Dayton Street Partners in 2022; Fujitsu now operates as 1Finity Americas and relocated its office last year to nearby Galatyn Commons at 2375 Glenville Drive in Richardson.

Celestica’s COO Yann Etienvre framed the move as a growth milestone, saying: “This expansion is a milestone in Celestica's growth strategy, allowing us to scale our advanced technology and manufacturing capabilities,” and adding that the company is “leveraging Richardson’s tech-forward infrastructure and top-tier talent to fuel innovation and support our customers' most complex needs.”

stories.name: Institutional Investors Boost Celestica CLS Stakes
stories.summary: Multiple institutional investors have been adjusting their positions in Celestica, including Arrowstreet Capital slightly increasing its stake and Storgate LLC initiating a new position, while Logan Capital Management raised its holdings. Other funds also added shares, and overall institutional ownership remains high at 67.38%. Not all activity is bullish: Sharpepoint LLC reduced its stake by 22.1%, and a Celestica director, Michael Max Wilson, sold shares in a reported transaction. Research coverage is mixed but generally constructive, with analysts raising price targets and reiterating or upgrading recommendations. Trading metrics cited for Celestica include a market cap of about $44.31 billion, a P/E near 46.6, and a wide 12-month range between roughly $124.72 and $474.02, with moving averages below the current quoted level.
keyPoints: Arrowstreet Capital Limited Partnership increased its Celestica stake by 0.2% to 3,152,285 shares after buying an additional 5,357 shares; the holding was reported as 2.74% of the stock worth about $931,966,000.
Storgate LLC’s new Celestica position was 4,235 shares (about $1,252,000) and represented 1.0% of its investment portfolio—described as Celestica being its 9th-largest holding.
Director Michael Max Wilson sold 4,168 shares at an average price of $333.31 for a total of $1,389,236.08; after the sale, he still owned 24,718 shares (worth about $8,238,756.58).

stories.name: Celestia token drops 18.2% weekly
stories.summary: Celestia (TIA) rose slightly over the past day but remains sharply lower on the week, down about 18% against the U.S. dollar, with its market capitalization around $45 million. The token is trading near $0.32, after a market-wide mix of minor day-to-day moves across related cryptocurrencies. Separate from the crypto market, Celestica (CLS) is drawing attention from investors and analysts following strong earnings and supportive commentary, despite recent short-term volatility in the stock. Capital World Investors reduced its Celestica stake by 3.3% in the fourth quarter, though multiple other institutional investors added positions, and institutional ownership remains high. Analyst coverage cited in the reports includes upgrades and raised price targets, while one valuation view places “fair value” above the recent share price, implying the stock trades at a discount. The bullish case is tempered by concerns that Celestica’s results depend heavily on a small number of hyperscaler customers and that changes in AI and cloud spending could pressure the outlook.
keyPoints: Celestia (TIA) has a total supply of 1,168,685,161 tokens, with 141,043,527 tokens in circulation, and it launched on Oct. 31, 2023.
In the last 24 hours, Celestia traded about $23.81 million worth of tokens on exchanges, and one TIA was quoted at roughly $0.32 (about 0.00000512 BTC) on major platforms.

Capital World Investors’ trimmed Celestica stake amounted to 632,443 shares after selling 21,702 shares; that position was valued at $186,957,000 in its most recent SEC filing. The company also reported that hedge funds and other institutional investors own 67.38% of Celestica.
